a study of positive self-evaluations in the course of a partially structured diagnostic interview.
the development of an interview technique for the elicitation of information about the self-concept.
a method of changing the way people describe themselves in a diagnostic setting.

the experimental procedure did not have the desired effect of increasing positive self-evaluations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
positive self-descriptions and evaluations are conditioned in a partially structured diagnostic interview setting and that this conditioning generalizes to a non-diagnostic situation.
the use of GSR feedback in a partially structured diagnostic interview can be used to condition positive self-evaluations in Ss.
the experimental Ss learned to self-describe in a more favorable way and to generalize this self-describing to a post-test measure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the feedback provided to Ss in a diagnostic interview is a powerful variable in the determination of the content of the self-description.
it is possible to use the diagnostic interview to elicit positive self-evaluations.
it is possible to use GSR to provide feedback to Ss in a diagnostic setting, and that this feedback may influence Ss' self-evaluations.
